$comment: The seating of a candidate in an office: the joint settlement of the recognition and induction predicates over that candidate — recognition the honor axis, reading backward at what the candidate has been; induction the munus axis, committing forward to what the office owes. Each axis settles to a Belnap charge, and the named states are read off the pair, never stored: vacant is (bottom, bottom); recognition-only and munus-only are the two half-seatings; dignitas is both affirmed; a top in either cell is a repair condition, held rather than resolved by overwriting. This class is the record that office.schema.json's no-holder rule points at: the office refuses to assert its holder, the character refuses to assert its offices, and the seat lives here as its own act — one incumbency, one candidate, one office. Hardened from office.schema.json's own $comment-absences (the double-settlement doctrine and its six named states), the install-an-officer work and duty, and keeping-the-personnel-register, which reads incumbency per office as exactly these two cells and records vacancy as vacancy.

office.$comment: The office seated into. Names an office and must resolve to one.

holder.$comment: The character seated. Names a character record and must resolve to one; whether a person or a session character stands behind the role is read from that record's kind, never assumed here.

recognition.$comment: The honor axis, settled as a Belnap charge: bottom is no evidence, t affirmed, f refused, top both held — a repair condition to surface, not a tie to break.

induction.$comment: The munus axis, same charges: the forward commitment to what the office owes, affirmed, refused, unevidenced, or contested.

from.$comment: The day the settlement was read. A seating is an act, and acts carry dates.

$comment-absences: No status key: vacant, recognition-only, munus-only, dignitas, failed, and repair are read off the two cells, and a stored state would be a copy that drifts. No until key: an incumbency ends by a later act that supersedes it, never by a field promising the future. No rights keys: the three rights a seated unit actually holds are the personnel register's readout, recorded right by right, refusing two-of-three rounded up to the set.
